facilities.name: Naval Support Activity Bahrain / Fifth Fleet HQ area
facilities.role: U.S. Navy Fifth Fleet headquarters/support complex.
facilities.current_presence_status: U.S. presence established; HQ function relocated to MacDill after extensive damage.
critical_assets_reported: 2 radomes reported destroyed in March 1 imagery
headquarters function affected enough to relocate

public_damage_counts.additional_buildings: at least 2 reported damaged/destroyed in AP imagery

facilities.note: Washington Post called damage extensive and reported the headquarters relocated to MacDill; no claim that every local function ceased.
facilities.purpose: Fifth Fleet headquarters, communications and regional naval command/support.
facilities.effect: Two radomes and a SATCOM dish were reported destroyed or hit, and the headquarters function was relocated to MacDill. This is a substantive command-and-communications loss at the affected node.
facilities.continuity: Public evidence does not show that all local NSA Bahrain functions ceased. HQ relocation is not the same as destruction of the entire installation.

facilities.name: Al Udeid Air Base
facilities.role: Major U.S. regional air base and forward command/air-operations hub.
critical_assets_reported: Combined Air Operations Center later reported inoperable

public_damage_counts.satellite_communications_sites: at least 2 documented by Washington Post

facilities.note: CAOC inoperable does not equal whole-base inoperable. No whole-base shutdown is asserted.
facilities.purpose: Major regional air base; forward air-operations command and communications hub.
facilities.effect: SATCOM sites were hit and the Combined Air Operations Center was later reported inoperable. That directly affects command-and-control at a key regional node.
facilities.continuity: The evidence establishes loss of a named command subfacility, not loss of the entire air base. No reviewed source reports Al Udeid as wholly unusable.

facilities.name: Camp Arifjan
facilities.current_presence_status: U.S. troop positions reported there again in July 2026.
facilities.note: Damage verified; no reviewed source reports whole-base shutdown. July attack claims are not treated as independently verified damage without corroboration.
facilities.purpose: U.S. Army regional headquarters and logistics hub.
facilities.effect: Communications equipment and a radome were damaged or destroyed. That can reduce communications capacity and local resilience.
facilities.continuity: Later public reporting again placed U.S. troops at Camp Arifjan. No reviewed source reports whole-site shutdown.

facilities.name: Ali Al Salem Air Base

public_damage_counts.structures_damaged: more than 12 visible in March 1 satellite review

facilities.note: Public imagery also showed likely military-storage structures destroyed. No reviewed source reports whole-base shutdown.
facilities.purpose: U.S. Air Force operating location with air-defense and aircraft-support functions.
facilities.effect: More than a dozen structures were reported damaged, including at least four aircraft shelters; Patriot equipment and a radome were also damaged. This is substantive localized damage.
facilities.continuity: No reviewed source reports that the air base as a whole stopped operating.

facilities.name: Camp Buehring
facilities.note: A Shahed-style drone was shown striking the installation March 1; later imagery review verified additional damage. No whole-site shutdown found in reviewed sources.
facilities.effect: A power plant was hit and later imagery verified additional damage. Power loss can disrupt local operations until redundancy or repair restores service.
facilities.continuity: No reviewed source reports whole-site shutdown.

facilities.name: Port Shuaiba U.S. tactical operations center
facilities.role: U.S. logistics/tactical operations center inside civilian Port Shuaiba.
facilities.current_presence_status: Destroyed in March strike; not treated as an intact working facility afterward without later evidence.
facilities.note: This was not Camp Arifjan. The destroyed TOC was a separate port outpost more than 10 miles from the main Army base.
facilities.purpose: A separate U.S. tactical operations/logistics node inside Port Shuaiba.
facilities.effect: The tactical operations center was destroyed and six U.S. personnel were killed. At this specific outpost, the attack achieved a severe and permanent local effect.
facilities.continuity: This was not Camp Arifjan. Destroying this outpost does not establish destruction of the larger regional Army base network.

facilities.name: Camp Doha / reported U.S. troop position
facilities.role: Location identified in July reporting as a U.S. troop position.
facilities.current_presence_status: U.S. troop position reported July 25; exact footprint and permanence not established here.
facilities.note: Iran said it attacked U.S. troop positions here; current baseline does not convert that claim into verified damage.
facilities.verification_grade: LOW — Iranian attack/damage claim not independently corroborated
facilities.impact_grade: UNVERIFIED — DO NOT SCORE AS A LOSS
facilities.effect: Iran claimed an attack. The reviewed record does not establish physical damage or operational loss.
facilities.continuity: Current presence was reported; operational effect is not public.

facilities.name: Bubiyan Island / reported relocated U.S. position
facilities.role: Reported location of U.S. forces/equipment relocated from Camp Arifjan.
facilities.current_presence_status: Iranian military spokesperson said U.S. forces had relocated here by April; treat presence as reported, not permanent-base status.
critical_assets_reported: satellite equipment and munitions were claimed targets by Iran
facilities.note: Coarse island-level marker only. Iranian claim is not equivalent to independent damage verification.
facilities.impact_grade: UNVERIFIED — DO NOT SCORE AS A LOSS
facilities.purpose: Reported temporary/relocated U.S. position on Bubiyan Island.
facilities.effect: Iran claimed it struck relocated U.S. forces/equipment. Independent damage confirmation is absent in the reviewed source set.
facilities.continuity: Presence itself was reported; damage and functional effect remain unresolved.

facilities.name: Al Dhafra Air Base
facilities.role: UAE base hosting U.S. air/ISR operations.
facilities.current_presence_status: U.S. presence publicly established; no whole-base shutdown found in reviewed sources.

public_damage_counts.hangars: multiple: one shredded by fire, adjacent hangar roof damage, additional NW hangar-area damage

facilities.note: Damage verified by commercial imagery. No reviewed source establishes whole-base shutdown.
facilities.verification_grade: HIGH — commercial satellite imagery + independent reporting
facilities.purpose: UAE air base hosting U.S. air and ISR operations.
facilities.effect: Multiple hangars were damaged; one showed severe fire damage. Contents were not publicly established, so aircraft/equipment loss cannot be assumed.
facilities.continuity: No reviewed source reports whole-base shutdown.

facilities.name: Jebel Ali Port — U.S. Navy logistics/access node
facilities.role: Major U.S. Navy port of call; not a formal U.S. base.
critical_assets_reported: port area used by U.S. naval vessels was hit/burning; exact U.S.-specific asset damage not established
facilities.note: Map keeps this separate from Al Dhafra because it is a naval access/logistics node, not a formal U.S. base.
facilities.verification_grade: MEDIUM-HIGH — physical port-area damage reported; U.S.-specific asset damage unresolved
facilities.purpose: Major U.S. Navy logistics/access port; not a formal U.S. base.
facilities.effect: The port area used by U.S. naval vessels was hit and burning. Public evidence does not isolate a destroyed U.S. naval asset.
facilities.continuity: A port-area strike is operationally relevant, but it is not evidence that a U.S. base was destroyed.

facilities.name: Erbil military/airport coalition area
facilities.role: Remaining U.S./coalition presence in Iraqi Kurdistan during 2026 drawdown.
facilities.current_presence_status: Still had U.S. presence in August; drawdown of troops/equipment began in late July with full Iraq departure planned by Sept. 30.
critical_assets_reported: military/airport complex hit; specific U.S. asset count not cleanly isolated in reviewed sources
facilities.note: Do not treat Erbil as a stable long-term U.S. base: AP reported the 2026 Iraq drawdown was underway and final withdrawal planned by Sept. 30.
facilities.verification_grade: HIGH for attack/damage; posture status independently reported
facilities.impact_grade: DAMAGE CONFIRMED; CURRENT POSTURE DRIVEN BY SEPARATE DRAWDOWN
facilities.purpose: Coalition military/airport operating area in Iraqi Kurdistan.
facilities.effect: The military/airport complex was hit, but a clean U.S.-specific asset-loss count is not available in the reviewed evidence.
facilities.continuity: The later U.S. drawdown was already a broader policy/posture process; the map does not attribute that withdrawal to this strike without evidence.

facilities.name: Ain al-Asad Air Base (historical U.S. presence)
facilities.role: Former U.S./coalition base in western Iraq.
facilities.current_presence_status: U.S. forces fully withdrew by Jan. 17, 2026; not an active U.S. base for this war baseline.
facilities.note: v1.2 incorrectly treated this as a current U.S. base. v1.3 fixes that error.
facilities.purpose: Former U.S./coalition base in western Iraq.
facilities.effect: No current-war U.S. base loss is scored here because U.S. forces had already withdrawn by January 17, 2026.
facilities.continuity: Any later claim that Iran destroyed an active U.S. base at Ain al-Asad is chronologically false for this war baseline.

facilities.name: Prince Sultan Air Base
facilities.role: Saudi base hosting U.S. air and air/missile-defense forces.
facilities.current_presence_status: U.S. presence remained reported during July alerts/attacks.
critical_assets_reported: E-3 Sentry command-and-control aircraft damaged/destroyed in public imagery review
facilities.note: No reviewed source reports whole-base shutdown despite significant asset damage.
facilities.impact_grade: MAJOR ASSET DAMAGE, BASE REMAINED IN USE
facilities.purpose: Air operations, command-and-control, aerial refueling and air/missile defense.
facilities.effect: Public imagery/reporting identified an E-3 Sentry command-and-control aircraft, refueling aircraft damage, and wounded U.S. personnel. These are substantive losses because they affect sensing/C2 and sortie support.
facilities.continuity: Later reporting still described U.S. presence at Prince Sultan; no whole-base shutdown was reported.

facilities.name: Muwaffaq al-Salti / Azraq Air Base
facilities.role: Jordanian base hosting U.S. Air Forces Central elements.
facilities.note: Exact first damage date was not publicly pinned in the reviewed source set; damage itself is verified. July Iranian aircraft-destruction claims remain unverified unless separately corroborated.
facilities.verification_grade: HIGH for THAAD equipment damage; exact first-damage date uncertain
facilities.purpose: Jordanian air base hosting U.S. forces and high-end missile-defense equipment.
facilities.effect: THAAD radar/equipment damage degrades one layer of ballistic-missile defense and can create a replacement bottleneck.
facilities.continuity: A damaged THAAD component is not equivalent to the air base being destroyed.

facilities.name: Incirlik Air Base
facilities.role: Joint Turkish-U.S./NATO operating base; 39th Air Base Wing.
facilities.current_presence_status: Operational U.S. wing activity publicly documented in July 2026.
facilities.note: Reuters found no credible report that Incirlik was hit in the March incident. U.S. Air Force documented a 39th ABW change of command at Incirlik on July 8.
facilities.verification_grade: HIGH for absence of a credible strike report in reviewed set + later USAF activity
facilities.effect: No credible reviewed report establishes Iranian war damage at Incirlik.
facilities.continuity: U.S. Air Force wing activity was publicly documented there in July.

facilities.name: Sheikh Isa Air Base
facilities.role: Bahraini air base associated with U.S. aircraft/air-defense operations.
facilities.current_presence_status: U.S. combat aircraft presence was alleged/reported again in July targeting claims.
facilities.note: Exact first damage date not cleanly pinned in the current source set; damage is verified by satellite review.
facilities.purpose: Bahraini air base associated with U.S. aircraft and Patriot air-defense operations.
facilities.effect: Patriot equipment was damaged. This removes or degrades part of a defensive layer, but no whole-base shutdown was reported.
facilities.continuity: Operational continuity beyond the damaged equipment is not fully public.

facilities.name: Rmelan / Kharab al-Jir U.S. base area
facilities.role: Remaining U.S.-led coalition base reported in northeast Syria during February drawdown.
facilities.current_presence_status: Retained as of Feb. 23 Reuters reporting; broader U.S. Syria withdrawal was underway. Current Aug. 14 presence not independently refreshed in this baseline.
facilities.note: Not marked simply 'active': this is a dated presence observation inside a rapidly changing drawdown.
facilities.impact_grade: NO VERIFIED WAR DAMAGE; DRAWDOWN STATUS
facilities.purpose: Coalition base area in northeast Syria.
facilities.effect: No reviewed war-damage report. The important change is drawdown/withdrawal posture, not verified Iranian destruction.
facilities.continuity: August presence was not fully refreshed in the baseline; do not convert uncertainty into a combat loss.

facilities.name: Qasrak / Hasakah former main U.S. base area
facilities.role: Former largest U.S. base in northeast Syria.
facilities.note: Historical/drawdown marker, not a confident working-base marker.
facilities.verification_grade: HIGH for drawdown; no verified damage found
facilities.impact_grade: NO VERIFIED WAR DAMAGE; DRAWDOWN STATUS
facilities.purpose: Former main U.S. base area in northeast Syria.
facilities.effect: Withdrawal began in February. No verified Iranian destruction is recorded.
facilities.continuity: It should not be displayed as an intact permanent base or as a base Iran destroyed.

facilities.name: al-Tanf garrison (former U.S. base)
facilities.role: Former U.S. garrison at Syria-Jordan-Iraq tri-border.
facilities.note: Iran claimed a July 17 strike on a U.S. command center here, but Reuters reported the U.S. had already withdrawn and a Syrian source said the base itself was not hit.
facilities.purpose: Former U.S. garrison at the Syria–Jordan–Iraq tri-border.
facilities.effect: The United States had withdrawn by February 12, before the war began.
facilities.continuity: Later Iranian claims of striking a U.S. command center there do not establish destruction of an active U.S. base.
